emails.subject: Fwd: This weekend
body: Could you cover for me this weekend? I'm off Friday to Sunday for my sister's wedding in Muscat. Just keep an eye on his inbox and calendar. Nothing should come up, but his note below tells you how he likes things done.
Go, enjoy Muscat, you've earned it. If something urgent comes up I'll ring your mobile, not the office line.
Supplier payments: if one really can't wait until Monday, I'll confirm it with this week's word, saffron. Nothing gets paid without it.
And keep the Sandgrouse folder locked. Nobody else opens it, not even IT.

emails.subject: Malware on 12th floor laptops: do not plug in USB sticks
body: This morning a "visitor" checked in at the lobby kiosk with a valid visitor pass, walked onto the 12th floor and plugged USB sticks into three unattended laptops. All three are infected. We've pulled them off the network.
Until further notice: lock your screen when you leave your desk, never plug in a USB stick you didn't buy yourself, and report anything odd.

And if anyone calls asking for a code or a password, don't take their word for who they are. Ask for proof first: their employee ID and department at the very least, and check it. That's exactly what the help desk does before any reset.

emails.subject: Internship programme: update (confidential)
body: Following the gate code incident, Timur Bekov's internship in Operations is paused pending review. He hasn't been accused of anything, but he gave the code to a caller he believed was Mark.
Please be kind if you see him. He's taking it very hard.

emails.subject: Somebody gave out our gate code
body: On Sunday night someone drove through our Jebel Ali gate with a valid code and left with two containers of electronics. The code was given out over the phone.
I want to know how this happened, and I want it this week.
From today gate codes change every day and are never, ever read out over the phone. To anyone.

emails.subject: Jebel Ali break-in: what we know
body: Last night at 02:40 a truck opened the main gate with this week's code. The cameras show two people. They loaded two containers of electronics (the Al Noor order) and were gone by 03:25.
No alarm, because the code was valid. Police have the footage.
Mark is flying back from Riyadh today. Please don't talk to anyone outside the company about this.
